rows.en: Fight Tsuda
Stay still
Call the nurse for help

"...What's wrong, Hosoda?
I never thought you'd end up in the hospital too.
But it's nice that our beds are right next to each other, huh?"
He said that and smiled.
He seemed somehow different from the Tsuda of a moment ago.
So I worked up my nerve and asked him.{p}

"...Hey, Tsuda.
Do you ever feel like you want to eat me?"
Tsuda just stared at me blankly.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Ah ha ha ha...
What are you saying, Hosoda?
Have you gone crazy or something?"
The Tsuda laughing in front of me was the usual Tsuda.
He didn't have that look.
I was so relieved I let out a long sigh.
And then Tsuda suddenly turned serious and said this.{p}

"...You know, I can't remember the last few days.
I wonder what happened to me.
I went to that restroom beside the gym, and a joro spider got on my shoulder there...
After that, I don't remember a thing.
And when I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.
Weird, right?"
As if his words were prompting me, I found myself nodding.
And I kept what I'd seen on the roof and what happened in the nurse's office to myself.
I mean, I didn't think Tsuda would believe me if I told him all that.{p}

I think Tsuda was probably being controlled by the joro spider.
Of course, I didn't tell him that either.
Well, Tsuda was back to normal, after all.
Case closed, as they say.
Tsuda still comes to school like normal, even now.
He's doing just fine.
It's just that sometimes, when he sees a fly, he gets that look in his eyes and licks his lips like it looks delicious.
And sometimes when Tsuda opens his mouth wide to laugh, thread comes spewing out of it...
But I'm not scared anymore.
That sort of thing is just a minor aftereffect.
In exchange, Tsuda now wolfs down everything like it's delicious, and he isn't scared of bugs anymore either.{p}
So, what do you think, {a}{f:|}?{p}Now will you believe the story about that restroom?
I believe it
I don't believe it
I might believe it if I met Tsuda

...You're a suspicious one, aren't you?
All right.
Then I'll bring him along sometime.
But I think you'd better believe in the curse of the bugs, at least.
If you keep killing things just because they're bugs, you'll be cursed for sure.
Bugs are alive too, you know.
At least remember that much for me.{p}

...And that's the end of my story.
...The seventh person still hasn't come, huh.
That means the next one is finally the last.
{a}{f:|}, I hope nothing happens.
...Because I think you're starting to notice it too.
The eerie aura that's enveloping this room.{p}

I see, that's nice.
Usually, if you don't go near them, they shouldn't do anything to you either.
That's the most peaceful way, isn't it?
I wish everyone were like that.
There are lots of people in this world who aren't satisfied unless they kill.
The guy I'm about to tell you about was exactly like that.
He was the type who, when he saw a bug, would chase it until he'd killed it.{p}

He tried to find the boss of the bugs, you see.
He'd decided all on his own that this mass outbreak of bugs was happening because some bug ringleader was giving the orders.{p}

One day after school, he went to that restroom to find the boss of the bugs.
And he took a stick and stirred it all around the restroom, where bugs were swarming in huge numbers.{p}

Bugs came welling up, as if overflowing, out of the toilets, the cleaning closet and the sinks.
Gradually the sun went down, and he turned on the restroom light and kept on searching.
The place felt less like a restroom than the inside of some unknown creature's stomach.
The floor, the walls and the ceiling were all rustling and squirming, as if they themselves were alive.
For the first time, he felt fear.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

He stood frozen.
He felt he finally understood how truly frightening the enemy he'd been trying to fight was.
But having come this far, he couldn't back down a single step.
By then he was half doing it out of sheer stubbornness.
"Wh-where's the boss of these things☆"
Unable to take it anymore, he shouted.{p}
Saying that, he swatted the moth out of the air with his stick as it flew at his face.{p}

From the shock of the blow, the moth fell to the floor with a splat, scattering its scales.
The moth's plump, swollen belly was cruelly crushed, splattering yellow guts everywhere.
For a while, the moth's wings kept twitching and jerking.
Watching it, he basked in a sense of triumph, thinking he'd defeated the boss of this place.
In the dim restroom light, the moth's scales glittered.
The scales drifted down like falling snow.
Just then, he realized his body was slowly going numb.
"...Damn, it's those scales★"
Before he could even finish saying it, he collapsed.
His vision slowly went dark, and his consciousness faded away...{p}
As his consciousness faded, all he could faintly make out in front of him was the crushed moth.{p}

They say he was found about three days after he died.
The cause of death was supposedly that he'd slipped in the restroom, fallen and hit his head in a bad spot.
But they say his body was in an incredible state.
Apparently...
From inside his half-rotted mouth, dozens of moths that had just hatched from their cocoons were flapping their wings open.
Circling round and round over his face, as if they were dancing.{p}

You can't imagine, right?
I mean, you can tell a guy like that isn't normal.
Normal people like us could never figure him out.
He tried to smoke those bugs to death, you see.
With mosquito coils.
{a}{f:|}, don't laugh.
People die from getting caught in the smoke in fires too, right?
It's the same with bugs.
He wasn't going to kill them all in one go.
He chose a way that would make the bugs die slowly, in agony.{p}

He took mosquito coils and snuck into the school in the middle of the night.
"...Making a fool of me.
...I'll kill you!
...Every last one of you, I'll wipe you all out!"
He kept muttering things like that, over and over.
The school at night is very dark.
And the fluorescent light in that restroom was broken, too.
It was dim even in the daytime.
At night, you couldn't see a thing.
As he got close to the restroom, he heard a rustling noise.
A scratchy, scraping sound, like things rubbing their bodies together, was coming from the restroom.
He left only the one exit he'd use to get out at the end, and sealed all the other windows from the outside with duct tape.
So the smoke couldn't escape.{p}
Holding his breath, he stepped into the restroom.{p}

Under the squishy stuff, he could feel the hard floor.
Without thinking, he shone the flashlight he was holding onto the floor.{p}

And the inside of the restroom was packed with every kind of bug imaginable.
And not just the floor, either, but the walls and the ceiling too.
It was less a restroom than the inside of the stomach of some unknown creature.
The floor, the walls, the ceiling, all of it was rustling and writhing as if it were alive itself.
For the first time, he felt afraid.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

He stood frozen.
He felt he finally understood how truly frightening the enemy he'd been trying to fight was.
But having come this far, he couldn't back down a single step.
By then he was half doing it out of sheer stubbornness.{p}

He bundled twenty mosquito coils together and lit them all at once with a lighter.
In the darkness, the lighter's flame lit him up red.
The coils caught, and smoke filled the air around him.
He scattered them all over the restroom and tried to get outside himself.
But the floor was slick with the body fluids of the bugs he'd trampled, and he couldn't walk properly.
He heard the bugs, reacting to the smoke from the coils, rustling as if they were writhing in agony.
It was a rustling like they were putting a curse on him.{p}

"Waaaaaah!"
Terrified, he screamed.
He struggled desperately to escape.
And then he realized.
The reason he couldn't move was that the bugs had caught hold of his legs...{p}

His legs were already buried in bugs up to about the thighs.
Unable to even move anymore, he was swallowed up by the bugs.
The next day, the person who found him was left speechless.
Duct tape was stuck all over the restroom, and it smelled kind of like incense, so they thought something was strange.{p}

"{f:Stop it|Please stop}!"
{f:I|I} was half shouting it.
I felt so sick I couldn't stand it{f:|}.
"Fine, I'm happy to stop here, you know.
{a}{f:|}, you must never use that restroom, no matter what...
I can't promise you'll be safe."
Hosoda said that and looked at {f:me|me}.
For an instant, {f:I|I} couldn't move.
Because on Hosoda's shoulder was a yellow-and-black striped... yes, that was a joro spider{f:|}.
There was a joro spider right there on Hosoda's shoulder{f:!|!}{p}

"Oh, this guy?"
With that, Hosoda let the joro spider out the window.
"Haven't you ever heard?
Spiders hold grudges.
My grandma always used to tell me that bad things happen if you kill one."
Hosoda went back to his seat.
"Well then, who's next?"{p}

Really?
You believe me, then.
That makes me happy.
I believe it myself, too.{p}

I really didn't want to.
But the teacher had called me by name, so I couldn't exactly say "I can't go with this person."
Not with him standing right there, either...
The two of us walked down the hallway awkwardly...
I prayed to God.
Please don't let him start saying anything weird...{p}

"...Hosoda, haven't you been avoiding me lately?
Do you hate me?"
Tsuda muttered it to me quietly.
Honestly, I never should have made that prayer to God.
"Huh? No, of course not.
What's this silly stuff you're saying?
Let's hurry up and get to the prep room."
I said it in a fluster.{p}

The prep room is full of all sorts of equipment.
The room is really cramped.
We'd been asked to bring back tripods, alcohol lamps and asbestos pads.
I quickly loaded the equipment onto a tray and tried to leave the prep room.
I felt I had to get out of that closed-in room even a second sooner.{p}

Then I saw Tsuda standing in the doorway, staring at me.
It seemed he'd been following my every move with his eyes the whole time.
With that look of his, like he was looking at food.
I backed away without thinking.
"I knew it.
What you said earlier was a lie, wasn't it?
You really are avoiding me."
Tsuda said that without taking his eyes off me.{p}

And then he reached behind him and shut the prep room door.
"...I'm so lonely.
And here I am, so fond of you.
I mean, you look so delicious.
Let's see... those pink cheeks of yours, for one."{p}

Tsuda was smiling.
On reflex, I tried to light an alcohol lamp.
...But it seemed we'd forgotten to bring matches, and I couldn't light it.
It's over... Am I going to become his food too, like those bugs...?
The moment I thought that, I heard a voice from outside.
"Hey, they said they want the other equipment brought over too."
It was a classmate.
I was saved!
I hurried to answer.
"I-I'm opening the door right now!"
I heard Tsuda click his tongue.
Somehow, I'd escaped.{p}

...After that, Tsuda stopped acting strangely.
He never attacked me again, and he never ate bugs again either.
But it seems he's still after me even now.
Sometimes he stares at me with a slimy, clinging look.
I'm sure he's trying to get me to let my guard down so he can make his move the moment he sees an opening.{p}

...{a}{f:|}.
If one day I suddenly stop coming to school...
you can be sure Tsuda had a hand in it.
When that happens, please, look into him.
And I want you to save me.
I'm begging you...
That's the end of my story.
Well then, shall we hear the next person's story...{p}

On reflex, I lunged at Tsuda.
I sat on top of him and choked him.
And what do you know, joro spiders came swarming out of his mouth.
I let go of his neck, shoved my hand into his mouth and made him throw up everything in his stomach.
"Urgh. Urghhhh!"
Mixed in with the contents of his stomach, a whole bunch of joro spiders came out, squirming.
And before those spiders could get away, I beat them to death with a slipper.
I still can't forget how that felt.
All the strength drained out of my body.
I'd killed the joro spiders, but I was worried about him, so I called out to him.
"Tsuda... Tsuda?"
He was coughing and hacking.
Maybe I'd gone a little too far just now.
But if I hadn't gone that far, who knows what would've happened to him... That's what I told myself.{p}

Tsuda turned to look at me.
He'd been choking, so there were tears running down his face.
Seeing him like that, I worked up my nerve and asked him.
"...Hey, Tsuda.
Do you ever feel like you want to eat me?"
Tsuda just stared at me blankly.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Ah ha ha ha...
What are you saying, Hosoda?
Have you gone crazy or something?"
The Tsuda laughing in front of me was the usual Tsuda.
He didn't have that look.
I was so relieved I let out a long sigh.{p}

I went to that restroom beside the gym, and a joro spider got on my shoulder there...
After that, I don't remember a thing.
And when I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.
Weird, right?"{p}

As if his words were prompting me, I found myself nodding.
"But hey, this mess around the bed... did I throw up or something?
That's so embarrassing, geez..."
He laughed cheerfully.
He really didn't seem to remember anything at all.{p}
I called the nurse for help.{p}

At the top of my lungs.
The nurse came running right away.
Thinking about it now, I should've just used the nurse call button.
But at the time, I couldn't think of anything like that.
"What's wrong★"
I told the nurse everything that had happened.
Of course there was no way I'd be believed... not with a ridiculous story like that...
I got a shot of tranquilizer.{p}

I don't know how long I slept, but when I woke up, Tsuda was no longer in the bed next to mine.
It seemed to be night, but it wasn't lights-out yet.
Which meant it was still before nine...
I was thinking things like that when I happened to look up at the ceiling.{p}

"★"
I strained my eyes and looked again.
I was sure that just now, a joro spider had been up there...
I spent the whole night without sleeping a wink.{p}

The next day, Tsuda came to visit me.
"Hosoda, are you all right?"
He said it looking worried about me.
I couldn't even look him straight in the eye.
...An awkward silence hung between us.
I worked up my nerve and asked him.{p}

...I see.
Thank you.
You believe me.
If it were a story I'd heard secondhand, you might not be able to believe it, but I experienced it myself, after all.{p}

Oh yeah, ever since then, Tsuda has had this weird mark on him.
He says it won't go away.
...It's shaped like a tiny spider, about the size of the tip of your pinkie.
Next time I'll bring him along and show you that mark.
Apparently, every month that mark moves to a different spot on his body.
I wonder if that's an aftereffect too.
Or else...
No, it's fine. I got rid of that spider back then, after all...
...And that's the end of my story.
Still, the seventh person sure is late.
Well, there's no point waiting forever.
If they still haven't come after the next story, let's just go home.{p}

I mean, you don't believe it, right?
I'll wait for you outside the restroom.
If anything happens, I'll come save you.
After all, experiencing it yourself is the best way to believe something.
Okay, {a}{f:|}?
It's a promise.
Well then, shall we hear the next story...{p}

Too bad.
The answer was a fox.
Well, to people like us, tanuki and foxes are pretty much the same thing, right?
Anyway, about why that restroom stopped being used.{p}

Once, there was a boy at this school.
Unfortunately, I don't know his name.
He had a strong sixth sense too.
In his own self-taught way, he'd look at everyone with what he called "spirit vision."
He loved fortune-telling, too.
There were always students crowded around him, wanting their fortunes told.{p}{a}{f:|}, would you want him to tell your fortune too?
I'd want my fortune told
I don't need my fortune told

{a}{f:|}, you know about Kokkuri-san, right?
Yeah, that thing where you draw a torii gate and letters and tell fortunes with a coin.
He was especially good at Kokkuri-san, you see.
And apparently his Kokkuri-san fortunes were often right.
But it's a dangerous thing, calling up spirits to tell fortunes.
To put it bluntly, it's low-level spirits that come down.
There's no way a high-level spirit would come down.
In the end, the only things that answer impure human wishes like that are low-level spirits trying to slip into the cracks in people's hearts...
And everyone does it half for fun. They've sure got some nerve, don't they?
Even my cousin did Kokkuri-san half for fun, and the spirit wouldn't leave.{p}

My cousin's family owned a small factory, but a little while after that it was driven into bankruptcy, and an employee in despair hanged themselves in the factory.
My cousin's grandpa went on the first shrine visit of the New Year and died when the crowd toppled like dominoes on the shrine steps.
And my cousin came down with some rare disease and died, just like that.
All of this happened within three years of my cousin doing Kokkuri-san.
No, sure, it might just be a coincidence.
But it's way too scary a story to write off as coincidence, isn't it?{p}

Back to the earlier story.
About that guy who was good at fortune-telling.
He went crazy too, you see.
The story goes that in his case, too, Kokkuri-san wouldn't leave.
They say he was like someone possessed.
He still came to school, but apparently he hardly ever went to class.{p}

And they say he often went to that restroom.
Maybe nobody was especially interested in him, but no one knew what he was doing in there.
A teacher apparently saw it: he'd drawn Kokkuri-san letter boards all over the restroom walls.
And he was laughing, holding a ten-yen coin.
Well, the way it ends is that he hanged himself in there.
The story goes that even now, a ten-yen coin sometimes appears out of nowhere and glides across the letter board on that wall.{p}

Still, that alone isn't very convincing, is it?
After all, I'm just repeating a story I heard from an upperclassman, word for word.
But you know, there's more to this story.{p}{a}{f:|}, are you interested in the rest of it?
I'm interested
Not really
All right, I'll tell you.{p}
